sourceType: Official Government of Punjab tourism website
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries are written in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: Northernmost Punjab district, where Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir meet. Gateway to Dalhousie, Dharamshala, Kangra, Chamba. Ancient name Audumbar; historically part of Nurpur State.

places.name: Ranjit Sagar Dam
places.facts: One of the largest hydroelectric projects in northern India, on the Ravi River; boating, sightseeing.

places.name: Kathlour Wildlife Sanctuary
places.facts: Shivalik foothills sanctuary with deer, porcupines, pangolins, reptiles, birds.

places.name: Mukteshwar Mahadev Temple
places.facts: Shiva temple with caves associated with the Pandavas' exile; large Shivratri and Mukesran Da Mela crowds.

places.name: Gurudwara Shri Barth Sahib
places.facts: Associated with Baba Sri Chand Ji, son of Guru Nanak Dev Ji.

places.name: Shahpurkandi Fort
places.facts: 16th-century fort built by Rajput ruler Jaspal Singh Pathania; associated with Ram Singh Pathania's 1848 resistance against the British.

places.name: Dhar Nature Retreat and Awareness Camp
places.facts: Eco-tourism site in the Shivalik foothills; camping, nature education.

places.name: Atal Setu
places.facts: Modern cable-stayed bridge, a major photography landmark.

places.name: Nurpur Fort
places.facts: Heritage fort of the former Nurpur rulers.

howToReach.air: Pathankot Airport (IXP), domestic, flights to Delhi; Amritsar international airport ~119km
